;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]], [[Afghan peace process]]
**The [[Taliban]] declares a three-day [[Eid al-Fitr|Eid]] ceasefire starting on Sunday. Taliban spokesman [[Zabiullah Mujahid]] orders all attacks to cease and only use force "if any action is taken against you by the enemy". Afghan President [[Ashraf Ghani]] welcomes the ceasefire and orders the armed forces of [[Afghanistan]] to "comply with the three-days truce and to defend only if attacked". [https://nationalpost.com/pmn/news-pmn/politics-news-pmn/afghan-taliban-declare-three-day-eid-ceasefire-from-sunday (''National Post'')] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-taliban-ceasefire/taliban-afghan-president-declare-three-day-eid-ceasefire-from-sunday-idUSKBN22Z0UH?il=0 (Reuters)] 
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Second Libyan Civil War]]
**[[2019–20 Western Libya offensive]]
***Forces of the international-recognized [[Government of National Accord|Libyan government]] retake two military camps, Hamza and Yarmuk, from [[Libyan National Army|forces]] loyal to [[Khalifa Haftar]] south of [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/libyan-army-retakes-2-camps-from-warlord-haftar/1851647 (Anadolu Agency)]

;Disasters and accidents
*A [[multiple-alarm fire|four-alarm fire]] destroys a warehouse at Pier 45 at [[Fisherman's Wharf, San Francisco|Fisherman's Wharf]] in [[San Francisco]], [[California]]. More than 150 firefighters are able to contain the blaze and save both the [[SS Jeremiah O'Brien|SS ''Jeremiah O'Brien'']], a [[World War II]] [[Liberty ship]] that saw action on [[D-Day]] at [[Normandy landings|Normandy Beach]] in northwest France; and the [[USS Pampanito (SS-383)|USS ''Pampanito'']] submarine, which had six war patrols from March 1944 through early 1945 in the northwestern [[Pacific Ocean]]. [https://sanfrancisco.cbslocal.com/2020/05/23/massive-4-alarm-fire-erupts-at-san-francisco-waterfront-pier/ (KPIX)] [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2020/may/23/san-francisco-d-day-ship-fire-fishermans-wharf (''The Guardian'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
**[[China]] reports no new cases for the first time since the [[pandemic]] began, according to the [[National Health Commission]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-china/china-reports-no-new-coronavirus-cases-for-first-time-since-pandemic-began-idUSKBN22Z047?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine]]
**The [[Gaza Strip]] reports the first death from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], a 77-year-old woman. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/05/gaza-reports-covid-19-death-outbreak-fears-200523172108869.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*The [[Government of Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[Ministry of Internal Affairs (Ukraine)|Ministry of Internal Affairs]] confirms that independent member of the [[Verkhovna Rada]] [[Valeriy Davydenko]] has been found dead in his office in [[Kiev]] with a gunshot wound to the head. [https://www.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/ukrainian-lawmaker-found-dead-in-central-kyiv.html (''Kyiv Post'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]], [[Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**Thousands of protesters, mostly supporters of the [[History of the far-right in Spain|far-right]] party [[Vox (political party)|Vox]], participate in car protests in [[Madrid]], [[Seville]], [[Barcelona]] and other cities against the continuing [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] and the national [[government of Spain|government]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-52783936 (BBC News)]
